summary: Iter15 retest: verified poster.py fix. GET /api/campaigns/{id}/poster.pdf as influencer and as partner both return PDFs whose extracted text (via pymupdf) contains 'RRCLUB.ONLINE' tagline and coupon URL 'rrclub.online/c/CLUB-10', and does NOT contain any case-insensitive 'theclub' substring. Repo grep sanity (backend/*.py + frontend/src/**) confirms no 'theclub' remains in source. All 3 pytest cases pass.
critical_code_review_comments: poster.py:28 now derives tagline from the coupon link host via split('/')[0].upper(). Works, but a bit implicit — a small helper (e.g., tagline_from_url(link)) or reading FRONTEND_URL from env directly would be clearer and safer if `link` is ever malformed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter15 test file /app/backend/tests/test_iter15_poster_tagline.py uses pymupdf (fitz) to extract PDF text and validate poster branding. Reuse for future poster branding regressions.
rca_of_the_issue: Iter14 identified poster.py:28 hardcoded 'THECLUB.PT' tagline. Main agent fixed it by deriving the domain from `link` param (link.replace('https://','').replace('http://','').split('/')[0].upper()), so with FRONTEND_URL=https://rrclub.online, the tagline renders as 'EXPERIÊNCIAS PREMIUM · RRCLUB.ONLINE'. Verified via PDF text extraction for both influencer and partner poster downloads. Fix confirmed.
